Question: On a \(4\times4\times3\) rectangular parallelepiped, vertices \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are adjacent to vertex \(D.\) The perpendicular distance from \(D\) to the plane containing \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) is closest to
Solution:
Method 1: Compute the same volume with two bases

Relabel the three adjacent vertices if necessary so that \(DA=DB=4\) and \(DC=3\). These three edges are mutually perpendicular. The desired distance is the altitude of tetrahedron \(DABC\) when \(ABC\) is its base.

It is easier to find the volume using base \(DAB\). This is a right triangle of area \(\tfrac12\cdot4\cdot4=8\), and its corresponding height is \(DC=3\). Hence
\[
V=\frac13\cdot8\cdot3=8.
\]
Now find the area of the opposite face \(ABC\). The Pythagorean theorem on the box faces gives
\[
AB=4\sqrt2,\qquad AC=BC=5.
\]
Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(AB\). Since \(ABC\) is isosceles, \(CM\) is perpendicular to \(AB\), so
\[
CM=\sqrt{5^2-(2\sqrt2)^2}=\sqrt{17}.
\]
Thus
\[
[ABC]=\frac12(4\sqrt2)(\sqrt{17})=2\sqrt{34}.
\]
If \(h\) is the perpendicular distance from \(D\) to the plane \(ABC\), the volume formula now gives
\[
8=\frac13(2\sqrt{34})h,
\qquad h=\frac{12}{\sqrt{34}}\approx2.058.
\]
This is closest to \(\boxed{2.1}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

Method 2: Find the distance in a perpendicular section

Choose the labels so that \(DA=DB=4\) and \(DC=3\), and let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(AB\). The right triangle \(DAB\) has \(AB=4\sqrt2\). Since \(DA=DB\), its median \(DM\) is perpendicular to \(AB\), and
\[
DM=\sqrt{4^2-(2\sqrt2)^2}=2\sqrt2.
\]
Also, \(DC\) is perpendicular to the box face containing \(D,A,B\). Thus \(AB\) is perpendicular to both intersecting lines \(DM\) and \(DC\), making \(AB\) perpendicular to the plane \(DCM\).

In the right triangle \(DCM\), let \(H\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(D\) to \(CM\). The line \(DH\) is perpendicular to \(CM\). Because it lies in plane \(DCM\), it is also perpendicular to the direction of \(AB\). The intersecting lines \(CM\) and \(AB\) lie in plane \(ABC\), so \(DH\) is perpendicular to that plane. Therefore the required distance is \(DH\).

The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
CM=\sqrt{3^2+(2\sqrt2)^2}=\sqrt{17}.
\]
Compute the area of triangle \(DCM\) using its perpendicular legs and then using base \(CM\):
\[
\frac12\cdot3\cdot2\sqrt2
=\frac12\cdot\sqrt{17}\cdot DH.
\]
Consequently,
\[
DH=\frac{6\sqrt2}{\sqrt{17}}
=\frac{12}{\sqrt{34}}\approx2.058.
\]
The closest choice is \(\boxed{2.1}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
